glm.feedback:
## Findings

**1. Category: spec — Severity: high**
File: whole diff (notably absent: `.shipwright/planning/01-adopted/triage-help-texts.md`, `client/src/lib/triageHelpDoc.test.ts`)
Finding: The acceptance criterion "a reviewable help-text list sits in the spec folder" is only half-implemented. `triageHelpDoc.ts` generates the document and its comment references a committed copy plus a drift-detecting test, but neither the generated markdown file in the spec folder nor the `triageHelpDoc.test.ts` sync test appears in the diff. As shipped, no artifact exists for review and nothing enforces the generated doc stays in sync with `triageHelpText.ts`.
Suggestion: Add the generated `triage-help-texts.md` under `.shipwright/planning/01-adopted/` and the sync test (`UPDATE_HELP_DOC=1` rewrite mode) to the change.

**2. Category: bug — Severity: medium**
File: client/src/lib/externalApi.ts:271–274
Finding: `createTask`'s args type gains `fixNowForTriageId`, but the diff shows no hunk that actually places it into the POST body sent to `/api/external/tasks`. If the body is built field-by-field (as the server route reads `body.fixNowForTriageId`), the link will silently never reach the server, and every card/tile behavior in the spec fails. From the visible diff it's impossible to confirm forwarding; if it relies on spreading `args`, the interface comment would be the only mention.
Suggestion: Verify the request body in `createTask` includes `fixNowForTriageId`; if it doesn't, add `...(args.fixNowForTriageId ? { fixNowForTriageId: args.fixNowForTriageId } : {})` to the fetch body.

**3. Category: regression — Severity: medium**
File: client/src/components/triage/TriageItemCard.tsx:53–57 (removed exports), TriageCardActions.tsx:24–27 (re-added)
Finding: `PRIMARY_BTN` / `SECONDARY_BTN` were moved from `TriageItemCard.tsx` to the new `TriageCardActions.tsx`. Any existing importer of these constants from `TriageItemCard` (not visible in the diff) will now fail to compile — the components referenced in the old file (`PromoteModal`, `TriageHelp`, badge components) are plausible consumers.
Suggestion: Confirm no other module imports these from `TriageItemCard`; if any do, update them or keep a re-export in `TriageItemCard.tsx`.

**4. Category: edge-case — Severity: medium**
File: client/src/lib/triageBoardModel.ts:65–68
Finding: `matchesTile` short-circuits `e.item.revisitDue` to `true`, so snoozed-but-due items always appear when the "In progress" tile is selected — even though such items are parked, not in progress, and the `inProgress` count (line 100) only counts them if linked. A returned-due card that has no linked task will show a count of "0 items" under the filter yet still appear in the narrowed list, and the spec says the In progress tile narrows to items whose linked task is not done. This bypass is inherited from the "attn" logic where it made sense (due items surface regardless); for "prog" it produces an inconsistent count-vs-list.
Suggestion: For `tile === "prog"`, check `input.linked?.has(entryKey(e))` regardless of `revisitDue`, or exclude due items from the prog tile filter.

**5. Category: test — Severity: low**
File: client/e2e/flows/triage-fixnow-task.spec.ts:76 (`expect(page.getByTestId("triage-tile-prog")).toContainText("0")`)
Finding: The tile count comes from `listTasks({ projectId: null })` — all projects. In a parallel/isolated stack where other tests or seeded projects exist with Fix-now-linked tasks, the "0" and "1" assertions can flake, since the count is global while the test seeds one project. Also, `TriagePage` polls every 5s, so a stale count could assert "0" before the link task query resolves rather than truly proving the pre-state.
Suggestion: Scope the count assertions to the project's own card visibility (the per-card assertions already do this) or make the stack guarantee single-project state before asserting global counts.

**6. Category: bug — Severity: low**
File: client/src/components/triage/TriageCardActions.tsx:53 (`defaultReason={...}`)
Finding: The Resolve popover's default reason uses the task title captured at open time; if the task's title is later edited or the popup is opened before the task list poll refreshes the title, the prefilled reason reflects stale data. Minor, but the spec says the reason is "optional" and the prefill is an implementation nicety — acceptable, only noting that `defaultReason` re-seeds `reason` on every open, which also wipes a user's typed reason if the popover closes/reopens during a failed dismiss (error → close → reopen loses input). Behaviorally fine per spec ("nothing happens until Dismiss"), so low.
Suggestion: Only reset `reason` to `defaultReason` when `defaultReason` itself changes or on first open, not on every `onOpenChange(true)` — or leave as-is if the UX is intended.

## Overall
The core flow (link on task → validated server-side with a strict regex → per-project keyed lookup → card box/tile/Resolve + reason popovers) is well-designed and the e2e tests are behavior-driven, but the diff is missing two spec artifacts (the spec-folder help-text file and its sync test), and it must be confirmed that `createTask` actually forwards `fixNowForTriageId` in the request body. Ship-with-fixes.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
